title: Air India Extends Saudi Suspensions: Riyadh, Dammam to November 30
excerpt: Air India and Air India Express will keep Riyadh and Dammam flights suspended until November 30, 2026 and Jeddah until November 21, with free rescheduling or a full refund for eligible bookings issued on or before November 10.
body:
• NEW on November 13: Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will remain suspended until 30 November 2026, and flights to and from Jeddah until 21 November 2026.
  • The previous advisory had kept all three cities suspended until 14 November, so Riyadh and Dammam gain 16 more days and Jeddah gains seven.
  • If your booking was issued on or before 10 November 2026, you can reschedule once free of charge, subject to availability, or cancel for a full refund.
  • Revised travel must be completed by 14 December 2026 for Riyadh and Dammam bookings and by 5 December 2026 for Jeddah bookings.

Air India and Air India Express have extended their Saudi Arabia suspensions again, the airline announced on Friday, November 13. Flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam will now remain suspended until 30 November 2026, while flights to and from Jeddah will remain suspended until 21 November 2026, according to ANI reporting of the airline's announcement. The airline cited what it called the prevailing situation in the region.

The announcement was made in an official Air India Newsroom post on X on November 13. It replaces the timetable in the group's previous advisory, under which services to all three cities were suspended until 14 November inclusive.

What changed, route by route

Riyadh and Dammam have moved the most. Both were due to stay suspended until November 14 under the earlier advisory; the end date is now November 30. Jeddah, which was on the same November 14 date, now runs to November 21. No restart date beyond those suspension end dates was announced in the advisory reported by ANI, and travellers should not treat November 30 or November 21 as a guaranteed resumption date until the airline confirms services are operating again.

The two airlines are handling rebooking differently by brand. Air India guests may reschedule their travel to or from any operational Air India station in Saudi Arabia. Air India Express guests may reschedule to or from any operational Air India Express station in Saudi Arabia or Bahrain, the advisory said.

Who qualifies for free rescheduling or a refund

The waiver is tied to when the ticket was issued and when travel was booked to take place. Guests holding confirmed bookings issued on or before 10 November 2026, with travel dates up to 30 November 2026 for Riyadh and Dammam and up to 21 November 2026 for Jeddah, may take a complimentary rescheduling, subject to availability, or opt for a full refund on cancellation, according to the advisory.

There is a deadline for using a rebooking. For Riyadh and Dammam bookings, revised travel may be completed up to 14 December 2026. For Jeddah bookings, revised travel may be completed up to 5 December 2026. Passengers who booked through a travel agent should also check whether their agent needs to process the change, and everyone travelling in the window should act through the Air India manage booking page or the support numbers below rather than travelling to the airport on a suspended date.

How to get help

For assistance with rescheduling or refunds, Air India passengers can contact the airline at +91 11 69329333 or +91 11 69329999. Air India Express passengers can reach its support team at +91 124 6935600. Guests may also use the airlines' city booking offices, the advisory said.

Why the suspensions continue

ANI reported that the announcement came after Yemen's Houthi militia said on Friday it had carried out drone and missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, including Aramco facilities in Riyadh, a military cargo plane at Sharurah Airport and Khamis Mushait Air Base, while the Saudi-led Coalition Forces said they intercepted and destroyed drones in the Eastern Region and Riyadh. Those are claims and statements reported by ANI, not findings independently verified in the airline's advisory itself, which gave only the regional situation as its reason.

The Saudi suspensions have been extended in steps through October and November. The October 30 advisory had already moved all three cities to November 14, with an earlier waiver for bookings issued on or before October 30. The November 13 step is the latest extension, and its split dates — longer for Riyadh and Dammam, shorter for Jeddah — are the detail travellers need to check before rebooking.

What to do next

If you hold a ticket in the affected window, check which city pair and which end date applies to you, then choose between the free rescheduling window and a full refund before the revised-travel deadlines in December. If your travel is after November 30, the advisory does not cancel it, but the pattern of repeated extensions means checking your booking status close to departure remains essential.
